intro: When you search for a corporate accountant near me, you are likely looking for an accountant who understands the financial and tax needs of a larger company or group, not just a sole trader. You want someone local who can handle consolidated accounts, corporate tax and possibly audit preparation. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK accountant who can quote you directly for the work.
need_heading: What people searching for a corporate accountant near me usually need
need_lead: Here are some of the situations that bring people to this search.
needs: You run a growing company that now has subsidiaries or group structures and needs consolidated accounts prepared accurately.
Your company is approaching an audit requirement and you need an accountant who can prepare the accounts and support the audit process.
You are planning a transaction such as acquiring another business or bringing in investors and need corporate tax advice.
Your current accountant is not experienced with the international aspects of your business, such as overseas subsidiaries or cross-border transactions.
You want a local accountant who can meet in person and provide assurance work even if your company is audit-exempt.
context_heading: One key thing to understand when choosing a corporate accountant
context: In the UK, the term 'accountant' is not protected, so anyone can call themselves an accountant. However, titles like Chartered Accountant (ICAEW, ICAS or Chartered Accountants Ireland), Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA) and Chartered Management Accountant (CIMA) are protected, meaning those professionals are bound by their body's ethics, training and complaints rules. Only registered auditors can sign statutory audit reports, so if you need an audit, check that the firm is registered.

Every accountancy practice must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC. It is reasonable to ask which body supervises the firm, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and how complaints are handled. This helps you judge the firm's accountability.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Describe your company's structure, including any subsidiaries or group entities, so we can match you with an accountant experienced in consolidated accounts.
Mention whether your company requires an audit or is audit-exempt, as this affects the type of accountant you need.
Explain any international aspects, such as overseas operations or foreign ownership, so we can find someone with relevant experience.
Outline any upcoming transactions, like acquisitions or fundraising, that will need corporate tax or transaction advice.
State your preferred location or willingness to travel, since you are looking for a corporate accountant near you.
Include your company's sector and size in general terms, as some accountants specialise in particular industries.
questions: What experience do you have with group structures and consolidated accounts?
Are you a registered auditor, and can you sign statutory audit reports if needed?
How do you handle international aspects, such as overseas subsidiaries or cross-border transactions?
Which professional body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance, and how are complaints handled?
Can you provide assurance work for an audit-exempt company, and what would that involve?

faqs.q: Do I need a corporate accountant if my company is audit-exempt?
faqs.a: Even if your company is audit-exempt, a corporate accountant can still help with preparing accounts, corporate tax returns and providing assurance work. They can also advise on whether voluntary assurance would benefit your stakeholders.

faqs.q: How can I check if an accountant is qualified to handle corporate work?
faqs.a: Look for protected titles such as Chartered Accountant (ICAEW, ICAS or Chartered Accountants Ireland), Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA) or Chartered Management Accountant (CIMA). You can verify membership with the relevant professional body.

faqs.q: What should I ask about international aspects of my business?
faqs.a: Ask about the accountant's experience with overseas subsidiaries, transfer pricing, double taxation treaties and foreign tax reporting. They should be able to explain how they handle cross-border issues.
